scope: Pure CNV_STR_TIME and CNV_TIME_STR on supplied packed date/time data

reference_basis.documented: Conversion signatures, optional seconds defaulting to zero, invalid text writing zero, and GET_TIME table fields with year since 1980 and two-second increments
reference_basis.uncertainty: Printed year width and CNV_TIME_STR format are inconsistent; SET_TIME detail ranges disagree with its table; native odd-second, locale, whitespace and invalid-packed behavior are unauthenticated

implementation_choices.grammar: ASCII DD-MMM-YYYY HH:MM[:SS], exact digit widths, case-insensitive English months, outer whitespace, Gregorian dates in 1980..2107; invalid text writes zero
implementation_choices.packing: GET_TIME table: year since 1980 bits 31..25, month 24..21, day 20..16, hour 15..11, minute 10..5, second/2 rounded down 4..0
implementation_choices.integer: Reinterpret the packed 32-bit word as signed INTEGER; negative patterns for 2044 onward; signed numeric ordering across that boundary is not chronological
implementation_choices.format: Complete 20-character DD-MMM-YYYY HH:MM:SS with uppercase English months independent of locale; no timezone or epoch conversion
implementation_choices.outputs: Exact INTEGER or ordinary writable STRING with concrete capacity 20..254; validate before writing; no truncation or overflow marker; invalid decoded fields raise
implementation_choices.effects: Capture source value then target reference once; convert after captures; retain prior effects on error; direct/transitive FOR protection and ordinary frame cleanup
implementation_choices.names: Pythonic fallback procedures preserve internal routines, results/effects and ordinary declarations; legacy internal mode retains unsupported calls

retained_boundaries: Conversions do not acquire clocks; GET_TIME/SET_TIME use a separate explicit CalendarClock since 0.87.0; no controller clock access, timezone, locale discovery or native chronological ordering claim
No controller contact, native format/odd-second/invalid-packed equivalence or runtime acceptance
Ordinary initialization, signed integer ranges, ASCII/capacities, CONFIG/POSITION reference checks and resource limits; strict remains future work
